title: Season 1, Ep 3: The AI infrastructure architect
oneliner: Infra architects moving to AI must trade VM-and-Kubernetes thinking for GPU topology: H100 and GB200 architectures, InfiniBand and RoCE networking, and the LLM gateway.
says: If you are an infrastructure or infrastructure-solution architect provisioning cloud or on-premises environments, shift your focus to AI infrastructure architecture. If you have worked with Kubernetes and virtual machines, shift to GPU topology: understand NVIDIA's H100 and GB200 architectures, the InfiniBand and RoCE networking concepts, and how the LLM gateway works for provisioning gateway services.
explained: Why a whole new vocabulary? Because AI workloads stress different parts of the machine. Classic infrastructure is CPU-bound and scales by adding interchangeable VMs. AI training and inference are GPU-bound, and the binding constraint is how fast GPUs exchange data with each other - which is exactly what InfiniBand and RoCE (high-speed, low-latency networking built for GPU clusters) solve. GPU topology - how the chips are wired within and across nodes - decides whether your expensive hardware is actually used or idle.

The H100 and GB200 are NVIDIA's data-center GPU generations; knowing their memory, bandwidth, and clustering characteristics is the AI infra architect's equivalent of knowing instance families. And the LLM gateway - the front door to models - is where infrastructure meets governance and cost, which he details in the very next episode.
takeaway: AI infrastructure is a new hardware literacy: GPU generations, GPU-to-GPU networking, and the model gateway. VMs-to-GPUs is the core mental migration.
